figures.finding: In England, Wales and Northern Ireland the first £12,570 is tax-free and income above it is taxed at 20%, 40% and 45%; the allowance falls by £1 for every £2 of income over £100,000 and is gone at £125,140. Scotland sets its own six bands from 19% to 48%.

value.regionalLayer: Scottish Income Tax, set by the Scottish Government, replaces the UK bands for Scottish taxpayers' non-savings income

figures.applies: Tax year 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027; the 2025-26 bands (to 5 April 2026) are the same figures for the rest of the UK (not re-read for Scotland).

figures.finding: An employee pays Class 1 National Insurance of 8% on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270 a year and 2% above; the employer pays 15% above £5,000 with no ceiling. A self-employed worker pays Class 4 of 6% on profits between £12,570 and £50,270 and 2% above; Class 2 is treated as paid from profits of £7,105, and voluntary below (£3.65 a week).
figures.applies: Tax year 2026-27, category A employees and sole traders.

figures.finding: An employer deducts income tax and National Insurance from pay through PAYE by the employee's tax code (the standard 1257L gives the £12,570 allowance); a self-employed freelancer has nothing withheld and pays through Self Assessment once self-employed income passes £1,000.

figures.finding: A payer withholds basic-rate tax (20%) from payments to a non-resident entertainer for a UK appearance, film productions included, once the year's payments pass the personal allowance; it is a payment on account against the final UK bill, not a final tax. Payments made directly to film directors, and for copyright and royalties, are not withheld.

figures.finding: A creator of literary or artistic works whose profits come from selling works or from royalties may claim to be taxed on the average of two years' profits, on HMRC's 75% condition; profits from services (a performer's fee, say) do not qualify.

value.relief: averaging of two consecutive years' profits
value.condition: as HMRC words it: the difference in profits of one of the tax years must be less than 75% of the profits of the other tax year, or the profits of one tax year are nil

figures.applies: Self-employed authors and artists filing Self Assessment.

sources.said: A special relief is available for creators of literary or artistic works under which they can claim to add together their profits for 2 years and be taxable on the average of those profits if certain conditions are met.
The difference in profits of one of the tax years must be less than 75% of the profits of the other tax year, or the profits of one tax year are nil.
You cannot claim averaging if your profits come from the services you provide.

figures.finding: A freelancer must register for VAT when taxable turnover over the last 12 months passes £90,000 (or is expected to within 30 days), and then charges the standard 20%; a business based outside the UK supplying the UK must register whatever its turnover.

sources.said: your total taxable turnover for the last 12 months goes over £90,000 (the VAT threshold)
Standard rate 20% Most goods and services

figures.finding: The UK tax year runs 6 April to 5 April; the 2026-27 online Self Assessment return and the balance of tax are due by 31 January 2028 (for 2025-26, 31 January 2027), with a second payment on account on 31 July.

sources.said: You must submit your online tax return by 11:59pm on 31 January 2027 or you’ll get a late filing penalty
There is a second payment deadline of 31 July if you make payments towards your bill
